items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains unworthy people
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be carefully hidden in the mortal world among the lowest people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of people.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
The chapter is the fifth
items.inference: Therefore this marks the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has been gained through the lord of Kaulas' grace?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The known object is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: Therefore the speaker claims to have known the determination of Kaula through the lord's grace.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: Therefore the inquiry seeks both who the soul is and what its nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and can this be fully explained?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
A specific locus of dissolution is sought
The speaker requests a complete explanation
items.inference: Therefore the speaker asks where the soul dissolves and requests that all this be explained.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
That reality is partless and eternal
That reality is free from disease and stain
items.inference: Therefore that reality is defined by supreme, partless, eternal, and pure qualities.
uncertainties: The referent of saḥ is implied from context as the soul or ultimate reality.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction, and stainless.

items.question: How is the transcendent soul identified in relation to haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supremely transcendent
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also characterized as power and individual
items.inference: Therefore the transcendent soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supremely transcendent; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filled vital air abide within living beings?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
This air is present in living beings
It abides in all beings
items.inference: Therefore the breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam may reflect transmitted phrasing.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul upon merely leaving the body?
premises: The subject leaves the body
This leaving is described as mere or immediate
Upon that condition the subject is called supreme Śiva
items.inference: Therefore, upon merely leaving the body, that being is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and inwardly perceived according to tradition?
premises: Something is heard abiding in the ear
The goddess is addressed
It has come down through traditional succession
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is heard inwardly as received through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard within the ear, having come down through the traditional lineage.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing this knowledge have for the addressed goddess?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing alone is emphasized
The fair-faced goddess is addressed
items.inference: Therefore even mere heard knowledge is presented as efficacious for the addressed goddess.
uncertainties: The main verb or result is carried over from surrounding verses.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge that has been heard...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: A period of six months is specified
One should practice
The goal is an ochre state free from bondage
items.inference: Therefore one who practices for six months attains a renunciant state free from bondage.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to ochre robes or the ascetic state symbolized by them.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits result from this practice in terms of health and yogic association?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
Association with yogis is mentioned
Union or meeting with them occurs
items.inference: Therefore the practice yields freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: Therefore the practice of the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: What qualities must a recipient possess to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: Therefore the teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The precise sense of sarva+bhāva+upapannasya depends on doctrinal context.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
This essence originates from the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: Therefore the essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sambhavam is slightly compressed in the transmitted line.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The speaker refers to her body today
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: Therefore the body, once struck by ignorance, is now claimed to be pure.
uncertainties: deham appears in accusative form but functions as the described subject in this line.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious knowledge about overcoming time does the speaker now seek to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear something
The topic is the auspicious overcoming of time
items.inference: Therefore the speaker now wishes to hear about the auspicious overcoming of time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear about the auspicious overcoming of time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the possibility of destroying death?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
No doubt is asserted
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed
items.inference: Therefore the speaker assures that death can be destroyed and promises to explain how.
items.plain_english: I will tell you without doubt how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be afflicted at the source of nectar and essence?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar
The means involves the essence of juice
Even a wise person is described as burning
items.inference: Therefore even a wise person may suffer burning at the source of nectar and essence.
uncertainties: The physiological referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are esoteric.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may burn at the tip of nectar, by the essence of that juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the tongue and palate is prescribed?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is to be directed there
One should drink the breath slowly
items.inference: Therefore the prescribed technique is to slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink it in.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are said to be destroyed
items.inference: Therefore practicing this technique for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protection against venom is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: Poison is considered as a threat
Even a bite by great serpents is possible
Poison does not enter the body
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner is protected so that poison does not enter the body even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
